name: Cold Brew Blend
description:
Less Bitter, Smoother, Chocolaty, have it chilled!   A blend of Arabica and Robusta coffee beans sourced from plantations of Chikmagalur. Our cold brew blend which is roasted medium is specially designed to extract a full-bodied, flavorful, and low acidity when brewed cold. Once brewed, it will remind you of Dark Chocolate and a hint of caramel. 
  How to brew?  
 1. Take 100 grams of ground coffee and mix it with 1 ltr of cold water in an open container. Cover and let it sit undisturbed for 16-18 hours.  2. Filter the brew in a bottle or jar using a muslin cloth or cold brew filter paper.  3. Store the filtered coffee in the refrigerator. Consume within 7-10 days for optimal freshness.  4. When serving, add ice cubes, milk, and sweetener according to your preference.

name: Kolli Berry Estate
description:
Coffee Variety -  Arabica Beans   Post Harvest Process   - Washed   Roast level   - Medium Roast    Region   - Mudigere, Chikmagalur    Kolli Berri Estate in Mudigere, 30 km from Chikmagalur, a women-led enterprise run by Pranathi Shetty. The cup is clean, uniform, and marked by bold flavors that cut through with clarity and balance. Designed for everyday drinking, it carries both strength and refinement - dependable yet distinctive.  
  The coffee starts with a comforting malt-like aroma. In the cup, notes of dark chocolate take center stage, followed by hints of ripe prunes that add depth and sweetness. A gentle acidity brings brightness, while the rounded body creates a smooth and satisfying mouthfeel. Clean and well-structured, the cup showcases consistency from start to finish, ending with delicate traces of cocoa and dried fruit.  
  The coffee cherries were harvested at peak ripeness from farms located between 3,500 and 3,750 feet above sea level. After harvest, the cherries were carefully sorted, with all floaters and defective fruit removed before pulping. The parchment coffee was then fermented to break down the remaining mucilage, washed thoroughly, and slowly dried. This careful washed process helps preserve the coffee's sweetness, clarity, and uniform character in the final cup.

description:
Coffee Variety  - AA Arabica Beans  Post-Harvest Process  - Unwashed, Monsooned   Roast Level  - Medium - Light Roast  Region  - Chikmagalur, Karnataka  
 Monsooned Malabar - A Unique Specialty Coffee from India. 
 
 The arabica beans from Chikmagalur are transported to Mangalore, a coastal city in India. During the monsoon season, the beans absorb moisture from the coastal winds, causing them to swell and develop a pale yellow color. This process results in some of the most distinctive flavors found in coffee. This unique Indian practice has gained global recognition, and we are delighted to offer it to discerning coffee lovers in India. name: Wild Fig Co-Ferment
description:
Coffee Variety -  Chandragiri Arabica Beans   Post Harvest Process   - Wild Fig Co-Ferment, Washed Arabica   Roast level   - Medium Roast    Region   -  Kalledevarapura Estate, Bababudangiri, Chikmagalur   Some ideas begin not in the lab or the market — but underfoot. 
 This micro-lot was born not out of invention, but observation. One morning walk, somewhere between the canopy and the soil, a whisper of possibility stirred. Wild figs - soft, fallen, sticky-sweet, scattered the forest floor like little forgotten gifts. Not harvested. Not sold. Just there. Fermenting into the earth. 
 In that moment, something shifted. What if the forest had already done half the work? What if nature, in her quiet generosity, had left behind an ingredient that was both abundant and invisible, until you slowed down enough to see it? 
 This is that coffee. Grown under the shade of fig trees. Fermented not with fuss or fanfare, but with what was already given. The cup that emerged is rich, round, and quietly wild. 
 Roasted to a medium profile to coax out depth without losing nuance, this coffee opens boozy and heady, rum and raisins layered with brown sugar and dried berries. A hum of fermented fig threads through it all, grounding the cup.
